message.content: The largest planet that has been confirmed in our observations is the protoplanet **HD 100546 b**. It is still forming around its host star and has a mass of roughly 20 Jupiter masses—about 20 × the mass of Jupiter. Because it is a protoplanet, its exact size and structure are still being studied, and it may not yet be fully “planetary” in the traditional sense. In short, HD 100546 b is the biggest object we’ve found that is still in the process of becoming a planet.
